text:
sarah: Heads-up — finalizing the JSON logging schema and sampling plan for fleet telemetry. Need quick sync on alert tuning for SLO dashboards. TL;DR: new structured fields, rule-based sampling, and PII redaction guidance. Looking for :eyes: from infra/observability.

mike: SGTM. Can you paste the proposed schema and sampling rules here?

sarah: dropping a snippet of the schema we discussed (minimal example):
```json
{
  "ts": "2025-07-10T18:12:34Z",
  "service": "inference-runtime",
  "env": "prod",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "node_id": "gpu-0123",
  "gpu_model": "A100-40GB",
  "instance_type": "p4d.24xlarge",
  "request_id": "req_7f9a2b",
  "trace_id": "trace-12345",
  "level": "info",
  "msg": "generation completed",
  "latency_ms": 12.4,
  "model": "gpt-4o-inference",
  "kv_cache_hit": true
}
```

anna: Looks reasonable. A few notes: 1) add a top-level "redaction_marker" field to indicate whether message content was redacted, 2) include "sampling_decision" (rule id) so we can rehydrate later, and 3) keep an indexed "severity" alias for alerting.

mike: Agree with anna. For sampling rules I propose: errors & alerts -> 100%, warnings -> 20%, info -> 5%. Add conditional rule: if SLO burn rate > 1.5x for any region, bump that region to 100% for all levels for 30m.

sarah: implementation plan: do sampling at the collector (fluent-bit) so we can tag records with "sampled:true" and "sample_rule:"; then pipeline (es/loki) indexes sampled ones fully, and stores minimal metadata for non-sampled.

josh: a few concerns: 1) collector-side sampling loses raw payloads for non-sampled entries (we rely on the metadata for triage), 2) we need a reproducible random seed per request_id to ensure consistent sampling across retries.

anna: noted. We'll set sampler to hash(request_id) % 100 < rate. That keeps sampling stable across retries.

ops-bot: ALERT: slo-burn-rate-high (us-east-1) triggered at 2025-09-01T14:05:12Z — burn_rate=1.9, window=5m.

mike: This is the exact kind of event where the dynamic bump should flip on. We should verify the pipeline respects "bump-to-100" signals from alerts.

sarah: action items:
- anna: open schema PR with "redaction_marker" and "sampling_decision" fields and example mappings (due EOD) :point_right:
- mike: update fluent-bit plugin config and add hash-based sampler rule (staging test)
- josh: add a Grafana alert rule that sets a label "sampling_bump=true" on the burn-rate alert and emits an event to the pipeline API

mike: question: where do we store PII redaction rules? per-service repo or central ruleset?

anna: central repo (observability/policies) so infra teams can update rules without touching service code. Rules should support regex + named capture groups and a denylist for fields. Redaction should insert "[REDACTED_EMAIL]" style markers and set "redaction_marker" = true.

sarah: logging best-practices note: do not send full request bodies to logs for inference requests — only metadata (request_id, model, truncated prompt_hash). If teams need full traces for debugging, use the trace-store workflow which only engages after a debug flag and access review.

josh: on alerts/tuning: recommend three calibrations for burn-rate alerts — warning at 1.2x (5m), page at 1.6x (3m), and emergency if 2.5x (1m). Use burn-rate + absolute error budget depletion combined. This reduces noisy pages.

mike: +1. Also add suppression if the same region already has an ongoing incident ticket.

anna: I'll include a Grafana dashboard JSON that maps logs -> SLO panels and adds annotations when sampling bumps are active. Will add a lightweight Loki/ES query examples in the PR.

sarah: ok let's keep the rollout incremental: 1) schema PR + tests, 2) sampler in staging for a week, 3) bump wiring between alert manager -> pipeline, 4) full prod rollout with 72h watch.

josh: tagging @oncall for the 72h watch once we flip prod.

mike: :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks everyone — filing the RFC PR now.
